findings.description: The bucket defines no server_side_encryption_configuration, so objects (including the uploaded vendor roster) are stored without enforced encryption using a managed key of the account's choice.
No ACL is set and no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is associated with this bucket, so bucket/object ACLs or policies could grant public access to the report data.
The bucket has no logging block, so read/write access to archived reports is not recorded, undermining audit trails and detection of unauthorized access.
Versioning is not enabled, so object overwrite or deletion (accidental or malicious) is unrecoverable and tampering is undetectable.
The ledger export bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration, leaving sensitive financial export data unencrypted at rest by configuration.
No logging block is configured for the ledger bucket, so access to sensitive ledger exports is not auditable.
Versioning is not enabled on the ledger export bucket, allowing silent overwrite or deletion of financial records.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block guards this bucket, so a later ACL or bucket policy change could expose ledger data publicly.

The model artifacts bucket lacks server_side_encryption_configuration, so stored artifacts are not encrypted with a controlled key and could be read from underlying storage or copied without key-level control.
No public access block is applied, leaving the bucket dependent on ACL settings alone to prevent public exposure of model artifacts.
The runbooks bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration; operational runbooks often contain sensitive procedural and connection details and are stored unencrypted by configuration.
No logging block is configured, so access to operational runbooks is not recorded for audit or incident investigation.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is attached, so public ACLs or policies are not blocked at the account/bucket level.
The audit/log-delivery bucket does not log access to itself, so tampering with or exfiltration of the consolidated audit logs would go unrecorded.
The audit log bucket uses the log-delivery-write ACL but has no public access block, so log data has no account-level guardrail against public exposure.
force_destroy = true on the audit log bucket permits Terraform to delete the bucket and all retained audit logs without object-lock or MFA delete protection, enabling destruction of evidence.

A vendor roster spreadsheet (likely containing sensitive third-party/PII data) is uploaded from the repository into a bucket with no default encryption and no kms_key_id or server_side_encryption argument on the object itself.
